items.content:
Operation: Plague Star descends on the Plains of Eidolon once more from September 9 to September 23, across all platforms. Steal toxin from Councilor Vay Hek and the Grineer, destroy the boil and save Cetus before the Infestation can grow out of control.

What You Need To Do

Speak to Konzu in Cetus to undertake the Plague Star Bounty Complete the series of Bounty Missions to earn Operational Supply Standing for the Event Rewards

What You Need To Know

Bounties come with various requirements for completion that yield specific Rewards outlined below.

Tier 1:

Requirements: No prerequisites Rewards: Base Standing: 1,025 Bounty Bonus Completion: 25 bonus

Tier 2:

Requirements: 1x Eidolon Phylaxis + 1x Infested Catalyst Rewards: Base Standing: 3200 Bounty Bonus Completion: 75 bonus

Tier 3:

Requirements:1x Eidolon Phylaxis + 1x Infested Catalyst + Steel Path Eligibility Rewards: Base Standing: 3800 Bounty Bonus Completion: 100 bonus In thanks for your hard work, Nakak has some new Offerings pulled from elsewhere in the Origin System for you to claim:
  • Teralyst Prominence Sigil
  • Ostron Community Sigil
  • Rift Sigil
  • Two-Handed Nikana Maligna Skin
  • Umbra Forma (Built)

We’re back and sat from across the world! LIVE from Seoul South Korea it’s Devstream #197!!

Soulframe Creative Director, Geoff Crookes, Soulframe Associate Art Director, Rosa Lee, Warframe Creative Director, Rebecca Ford, and Community Director & Live Ops, Megan Everett, and South Korean Host, Will Chobra, are bringing you the first full reveal of our next major update: The Iceblade of Narin! 

Join us as we dive into the sEoul of Iceblade with the first reveal of our 66th Warframe, Narin, from her full ability kit to her deeper connection to a certain Cephalon. Plus all the details on Banshee’s Rework, a showcase of Qorvex Deluxe, Banshee Deluxe, and Citrine Prime. Due to the offsite nature of this Devstream, there will be no Twitch Drops. To circumvent this, we have added the Twitch Drop item as an additional Gift of the Lotus alert in-game that will go live when the Devstream concludes. Tune in for the details!

items.title: Amir’s Shockwave is Live!
items.summary: Amplify your Arsenal with all-new Rewards like the Globakk Syandana, Kaneshell Atomicycle Regalia, Teisatz Oculus and more. Prepare for a shift in the balance of power — as Amir’s Shockwave is now live! The hex hacker’s electric personality
items.content:
Amplify your Arsenal with all-new Rewards like the Globakk Syandana, Kaneshell Atomicycle Regalia, Teisatz Oculus and more. Prepare for a shift in the balance of power — as Amir’s Shockwave is now live! The hex hacker’s electric personality is amplifying this Nightwave Mix with all-new Rewards like the 1999-themed Globakk Syandana, Kaneshell Atomicycle Regalia, Teisatz Oculus and oh-so much more.

Fables & Frontiers: Running Late

Entirely separate from this new series of Nightwave Mix Rewards, there’s also the brand-new six-day KIM mini narrative adventure in the form of Fables & Frontiers: Running Late! Allow the mischievous technophile Amir to guide you through this bite-sized take on the Fables & Frontiers tabletop game from the world of Warframe: 1999. To unlock Fables & Frontiers: Running Late, you must complete The Hex Quest’s finale and reach Rank 5 with The Hex Syndicate and a KIM Chemistry of “Close” (Rank 5) with Amir himself. Earn several all-new Rewards from Fables & Frontiers: Running Late, including the Atomicycle Key Sugatra, Fables & Frontiers Glyphs for each member of The Hex, several returning items from Nora's Mix Vol. 8 and much more! All of these can be redeemed from Amir by ringing the bell in a new area of The Höllvania Central Mall in exchange for Hex Standing. Please Note: Fables & Frontiers: Running Late is a permanent addition to the KIM System that you can access anytime by meeting the correct prerequisites and is not tied to Nightwave Mix: Amir’s Shockwave.

What is Nightwave?

Experiencing this facet of Warframe for the first time? Nightwave is a pirate radio broadcast hosted by Nora Night (or, in this case, Amir of The Hex), focused on the latest stories in the Origin System. Nightwave is also a series of Daily, Weekly and now Acts. All of which offer new and useful (and often entirely unique) Rewards! Nightwave is available via the Base of Operations’ Navigation console, through the Orbiter’s radio scanner (located on the left side of your Orbiter’s bridge), or via the Pause Menu UI. In the Nightwave menu, you’ll see your progress through the current mix, your current Reward Tiers, as well as a rotating set of Daily, Weekly, Elite Weekly and Permanent Weekly Acts. Stick with Nightwave each day and get some fantastic Customizations!

items.title: Prime Resurgence
items.summary: Two iconic forces return to the Origin System! Baruuk Prime and Revenant Prime are now available in Prime Resurgence. Whether you’re a new Tenno beginning your journey or a veteran returning to battle, this rotation offers the opportunity t
items.content:
Two iconic forces return to the Origin System! Baruuk Prime and Revenant Prime are now available in Prime Resurgence. Whether you’re a new Tenno beginning your journey or a veteran returning to battle, this rotation offers the opportunity to expand your Arsenal instantly with Regal Aya.

Meet the Primes

Baruuk Prime A master of restraint, Baruuk Prime walks the line between pacifism and devastating force. Calm the battlefield, disarm your enemies and unleash overwhelming power when pushed to your limit. If you prefer a measured approach that can erupt into unstoppable strength, Baruuk Prime might be the Warframe for you. Revenant Prime An immortal force of Eidolon, Revenant Prime turns the power of his enemies against them. Mesmerize foes, steal their strength and become a chaotic presence on the battlefield. If you prefer to dominate your enemies and make their power your own, Revenant Prime might be the Warframe for you. Prime Warframes Want to learn more about Prime Warframes?

Check out our guide to Prime Warframes video for a helpful breakdown of what Prime Warframes are, different ways you can earn them and how you can purchase Prime items.

items.title: Dog Days 2026
items.summary: Get ready to soak up some summer sun, Tenno! Dog Days returns on August 4 , bringing back Warframe’s annual summer splash with new Rewards, gameplay adjustments and plenty of seaside fun. New to Dog Days? Welcome to the beach, Tenno! Dog Da
items.content:
Get ready to soak up some summer sun, Tenno! Dog Days returns on August 4, bringing back Warframe’s annual summer splash with new Rewards, gameplay adjustments and plenty of seaside fun.

New to Dog Days?

Welcome to the beach, Tenno! Dog Days is a summer celebration where everyone plays on equal footing. Complete Vor’s Prize and unlock Cetus to join the festivities, then dive into the action by taking part in the Main Event Alerts to earn Community Glyphs and accompanying Rewards!

How To Play

From Navigation, select the Dog Days Missions under the Event tab to be transported to a tropical arena that shifts from day to night. The Dog Day’s arena is a water munitions-only zone, which means there are no Mods, Buffs (Invigorations and Archon shards), Companions, or Abilities. Winning a match depends on who can drench the opposing team the most (Tenno vs. Grineer) before the timer runs out. Whether you’re a long-time veteran or a brand-new Tenno, grab your Soaktron and get ready to make a splash!

New Rewards

There’s plenty to look forward to when Dog Days returns, including new Rewards and cosmetics to add to your collection. Earn Nakak Pearls by taking part in the event, then trade them in with Nakak on Cetus for a variety of beachside goodies! Daybreak Domestik Drone: Log in during the event to receive this Inbox Reward. Community Glyphs: Take part in Main Event Alerts to earn Community Glyphs and accompanying Rewards! Daybreak Skins: Bring some extra summer style to your Arsenal with these new customization items. Honoria: Flaunt a new, summer-themed Honoria during Dog Days. Daybreak Domestik Drone: Log in during the event to receive this Inbox Reward. Community Glyphs: Take part in Main Event Alerts to earn Community Glyphs and accompanying Rewards: Alert 1: Community Dog Days Kela De Thaym Glyph + 50K Credits + 25 Pearls Alert 2: Community Dog Days Rusalka Glyph + 50K Credits + 50 Pearls Alert 3: Community Dog Days Erra Glyph + 50K Credits + 75 Pearls Alert 4 (Bonus): Community Dog Days Executioner Garesh Glyph + 50K Credits + (100 Pearls + 2 Pearls per kill) Credits to Community Artist @SpaceWaifuart for creating this years Dog Days Glyphs! Please note: Replaying Mission 4 earns you Nakak Pearls for each enemy you soak to smithereens, and now also for assists. Daybreak Skins: Bring some extra summer style to your Arsenal with these new customization items: Magistar Daybreak Skin Daybreak Dax Syandana Bubonico Daybreak Skin Daybreak Sugatra Kompressa Daybreak Skin Honoria: Flaunt a new, summer-themed Honoria during Dog Days.

Floaty of Fury Alerts & Double Affinity Weekends

Special Floaty of Fury Alerts will appear throughout the event, offering additional ways to earn Rewards and Nakak Pearls. August 6 - 10: Defense (Uranus) - 175 Nakak Pearls + 50K Credits August 13 - 17: Exterminate (Venus) - 175 Nakak Pearls + 50K Credits August 20 - 24: Interception (Jupiter) - 175 Nakak Pearls + 50K Credits August 27 - 31: Survival (Sedna) - 175 Nakak Pearls + 50K Credits September 3 - 7: Sabotage (Pluto) - 175 Nakak Pearls + 50K Credits Additionally, Double Affinity Weekends will be running at the same time as the Alerts to help make the most of your summer. Be sure to keep an eye on the Star Chart and don’t miss your chance to dive into these special Alerts!

Event Changes

Dog Days is making some waves with gameplay adjustments designed to make this year’s summer skirmish even more fun: Floaty of Fury Alerts: These special Alerts will now override your melee loadout with the Noodletron and lock you out of your equipped Primary and Secondary Weapons. To compensate, you’ll also benefit from increased melee speed as you take on the challenge. Soaktron: The Soaktron has received increased Projectile Velocity, letting you soak your opponents from even farther away!

Community Captura Contest

Think you’ve got what it takes to capture the perfect summer moment? Keep an eye out for an upcoming forum post with more details on the Dog Days 2026 Community Captura Contest, including rules, submission details and more. Whether you’re a seasoned Tenno or just getting started, there’s plenty of fun waiting for you when Dog Days returns. See you surfside, Tenno!

items.title: Destiny’s biggest rival Warframe has had ‘two years of massive growth’
items.summary: Digital Extremes believes in console growth, and discusses the ‘careful’ development of its second game
items.content:
Playback speed × Share post Share post at current time Share from 0:00 0:00 / Generate transcript A transcript unlocks clips, previews, and editing. 9 2 Destiny’s biggest rival Warframe has had ‘two years of massive growth’ Digital Extremes believes in console growth, and discusses the ‘careful’ development of its second game Christopher Dring Jul 28, 2026 9 2 Share Transcript Listen now on Apple , Spotify or YouTube In This Edition, Digital Extremes’ Sheldon Carter on…

Bungie’s ‘looter shooter’ Destiny was a real thorn in the side of Warframe.

The Digital Extremes game had launched 18 months earlier, and found itself facing off against a better resourced rival.

“There’s a lot of overlap between the two games,” says Digital Extremes president Sheldon Carter.

“Destiny 1 really hit us when it came out. It’s a looter shooter with tons of marketing and really great developers on the team. Destiny 2 as well.”

In May this year, Bungie announced the end of Destiny. It would no longer be making updates to the series. And since then, most of the Destiny team has been laid off.

“For a while we thought about [Destiny] as competition and we were aggressively wanting to compete with what they’re doing. But over time, developers from their team come onto our team. New people who we started, they learnt what looter shooters are because they’ve put thousands of hours into Destiny. And so, at our studio, it was a bit of mourning with that news. The mood was pretty dour.

“The budgets and the competition to keep putting updates out… it’s really difficult and every studio has its own culture and different way of doing things. I can’t imagine [what it’s like] with a studio as big as Bungie, which also had Marathon going on, and a lot of different things pulling them in a lot of directions. Honestly, for me, it’s more sadness that it’s over. I hope the best for all the people there.”

Sheldon Carter, Digital Extremes Warframe is in a very different position. Five years ago, Digital Extremes felt that the game had peaked and it began work on a new game, a multiplayer RPG called Soulframe.

“Some people in the company were like, ‘Oh, Warframe’s peaked. And as it gradually goes to the West, we will have to start something new.” And while we did start another project, we changed our focus about how we were developing Warframe, how we were promoting it, and we’ve had a few years of straight just massive growth.

“Now we’re in this happy position where Warframe’s really thriving, and that gives us the ability to give Soulframe a tone of rope to try stuff out.”

Keywords Studios is the games industry’s end-to-end partner, with over 13,000 people across 26 countries helping studios build, launch and grow games at global scale. Supercharged by technology and shaped by long-term partnership, Keywords Studios connects specialist expertise around the player experience.

For game development, that means flexible production support that scales with ambition. From co-development and engineering to live operations and technical delivery, Keywords Studios helps teams move faster, solve complexity and keep production connected, without losing sight of the game players are waiting for.

Although Warframe lacks the profile of Destiny, the game and its studio is still a significant operation. Digital Extremes, which is owned by Tencent, now has over 500 staff.

items.title: After years of failing to get into MMOs, Warframe finally won me over in 2026
items.content:
Digital Extremes' sci-fi game has finally ensnared me, and I'm now even more excited for Soulframe

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works .

(Image credit: Digital Extremes) {alert('Link copied')}).catch(err => {console.error('Failed to copy: ', err)})" data-platform="copy_link" data-action="" class="font-ui-heading py-2 text-sm text-neutral-700 hover:bg-neutral-100 transition-colors no-underline block cursor-pointer border-0 bg-transparent w-full text-left normal-case" aria-label="Copy link" role="menuitem" data-analytics-id="article-social" analytics-label="utility-bar-social-share-copy-link" analytics-name="utility-bar-secondary" data-mrf-recirculation="article-social"> Copy link Facebook X Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 0 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter Until I played Warframe , the MMO had always been a hard sell for me. The constant updates and endless narrative expansions as seen in World of Warcraft and Final Fantasy 14 intimidate like nothing else in the video game world. I almost always crave the comfort of knowing I'm progressing towards a logical end point – at least when it comes to story-driven games – and the best MMOs , as a rule, seek to go on for eternity.

So despite my efforts, games like Black Desert Online, Fallout 76 , and Genshin Impact lose me soon after I start, simply because I can't accept the potentially limitless experiences on offer. How am I supposed to feel satisfied with my progress if there's no end destination? Well, one game recently changed my mind.

I first tried Warframe over a decade ago on Xbox One but quickly bounced off it. This was a different time in my life, before I could appreciate single-player live service games like Diablo 4 and arguably Fortnite . Even the original Destiny didn't hold my attention, so maybe it was a sci-fi thing? No, that wasn't it – what futuristic FPS could compare to Titanfall back in the day? Or now, for that matter?

But when I went to TennoCon earlier this month, I saw Digital Extremes' long-running epic in a whole new light. The game's community is held in high regard, and it was almost immediately clear as to why. The fans attending the convention were enthusiastic, friendly and generous, praising cosplays and handing out stickers in the name of Warframe and Soulframe, the latter being Digital Extremes' latest work currently in early access on PC only.

As I breathed in the atmosphere, I knew I had to try Warframe again – so I installed the free-to-play title on my Xbox Series X when I got home and jumped in. I chose my first playable biomech warframe (Volt, if you're curious), and began exploring the numerous planets, enemies and loot all crying out for my undivided attention.

Warframe head's advice for live service devs is to "make a good game before they kick you out" Guild Wars 3 may have cracked the MMO code for tired millennials In a world filled with live service games, MMORPGs are finding new ways to flourish (War)frame of Mind Unlike many of the new games I've been playing in recent years, Warframe is 100% a power fantasy. Right out of the gate, I was blasting foes to bits with firearms, cleaving through them with blades, and electrocuting them with my warframe's unique abilities.

It all felt wonderful. There was no immediate challenge like Elden Ring , or intrinsic sense of vulnerability like Resident Evil Requiem (the Grace sections, anyway). This isn't to say I don't enjoy FromSoftware and Capcom games – because I do – but the change of pace is refreshing in 2026.

Weekly digests, tales from the communities you love, and more

(Image credit: Digital Extremes) (Image credit: Digital Extremes) (Image credit: Digital Extremes) (Image credit: Digital Extremes) Image 1 of 4 View Original

As for the all-important narrative element that usually leaves me frustrated in an MMO, I was saved from my usual despair by simply not knowing what was happening. This tracked with what creative director Rebb Ford told GamesRadar+ when we interviewed her recently: "You will have no idea what's going on, and that's okay," she said with a smile, and she was right on the money. Luckily for me, the old adage of 'ignorance is bliss' rang true, because I was having too much fun dishing out damage to care who or what a Tenno was.

So why couldn't I stop worrying and learn how to love the MMO before? In truth, I don't entirely know, but the satisfyingly slick combat and traversal of Warframe certainly plays a part. Each time I begin a mission, I hurl my warframe head-first into the mayhem, shooting, slicing and ability-ing my way through the enemy hordes without a care for why I'm doing it. Yes, I have the guiding voice of Lotus, the game's matriarchal figure (and voiced by Rebb Ford), for support, but I don't pay too much mind to the why , merely the what ..

And yet, my mind wanders from time to time. I think about Lotus, Teshin, and the other NPCs I've made contact with in Digital Extremes' universe, and I want to know their histories, motivations, hopes, and everything else about them. The thing is, I'm in no rush. Warframe has enough content to keep players occupied for a long time – between 114 and 1,556 hours according to How Long to Beat – so I'll find the answers when I'm ready.

TennoLive 2026 swept us away beyond the boundaries of the Origin System to far-flung Tau and the smoky gambling dens of Fornax. Doomy, gloomy, yet undeniably stylish, our Gameplay Demo's seductive allure was all the more potent thanks to the sultry sounds of a particular musical number sung by Sentient crooner Larynde. We know how difficult it can be to keep such a beautifully brooding ballad out of one's head, so we've made it available to stream anytime you'd like through your platform of choice. If you haven't heard it yet (or just want an immediate re-listen), the visualizer for "View From The Top" is also now available on the YouTube Channel.

Conceived, performed and produced in-house by Warframe's unstoppable sound team, this might just be our most cinematic soundscape yet. Let us know what you think on our social channels, and please enjoy!

Warframe: Mesa Prime Build and Review
items.summary: Mesa is a legacy warframe that has stood the test of time over the years, here is our recommended build and review for her.
items.content:
Mesa and her Prime have been in Warframe for a very long time, and at this point in the game, are still considered the most mainstream, strong, and fun frames out there. There are plenty of reasons for this. Mesa can shield herself, buff her allies, and, with the right build, mow down legions of foes with ease. Below will be our recommended build for her Prime you can try out. Followed by our review of how she’s held up over the years!

Below will be the build for her Prime, which you will need 0 formas for. Her normal version will need 2 formas:

Below will be the build for her Regulators, which you will need 1 forma for with either her normal or Prime version:

Let’s start with the main build. You will want to stack everything into power, strength, duration, and efficiency. Mesa needs her abilities to work as long as they can and to be re-castable as much as possible. Obviously, the main draw for power strength will be for her regulators, which you will need Mesa’s Waltz for mobility. Her regulators are her main damage-dealing ability. They auto target, have crazy good stats, and with Secondary Enervate , you can at least get constant orange critical hits with them.

Finally, my choices for her Archon Shards are down below. You can change these out for whatever you see fit in your playstyle.

Mesa in Warframe has really stood the test of time. To my knowledge, she is one of the only frames that has not received a full-on rework, nor does she need one. I mean, that didn’t stop Digital Extremes from reworking Nova back in the day when she was perfect as is, but still. She’s strong, crazy strong, and very durable in missions. You need Mesa’s Waltz to stay mobile and avoid death as much as possible. But with the above build, you can take any difficulty with her and shine brightly with her.

items.title: Warframe is showing love to tabletop games with this ‘legally distinct’ RPG
items.summary: Amir finally gets to play Fables & Frontiers this August
items.content:
on Google Preferred Source Google News Link copied to clipboard By Simone de Rochefort Published Jul 11, 2026, 6:01 PM EDT Gaming Amir finally gets to play Fables & Frontiers this August

Image: Digital Extremes Warframe Sign in to your Polygon.com account Add Us Add on Google Preferred Source Google News Summary Generate a summary of this story Like Like follow Follow followed Followed Thread Log in Here is a fact-based summary of the story contents: Try something different: Show me the facts Explain it like I’m 5 Give me a lighthearted recap Dungeons & Dragons is in the air at Digital Extremes. The developer is introducing a new minigame to Warframe : a “legally distinct” roleplaying game called Fables & Frontiers .

Longtime players will recognize the name. It’s the fantasy tabletop game that Amir, one of the 1999 expansion protoframes, desperately wants to play with the rest of the Hex. Well, it’s finally time for Amir’s dream of playing a game with his friends to come true.

“This particular mini adventure is staying forever as a permanent expansion to the Hex,” Warframe creative director Rebecca Ford told Polygon in a pre-TennoCon 2026 interview. “What we found was as we move away from 1999 , year over year, it's just too important to leave.”

Warframe: 1999 expanded the human cast of the game for the first time, introducing protoframes that hold the line for humanity against an alien infestation. Also, you can kiss them . Now the game’s narrative is pushing toward a new star system with the upcoming Tau expansion, but the protoframes are beloved characters whose stories still matter to the community.

Image: Digital Extremes “People for a long time have been like, ‘When is Amir ever gonna play [...] Fables & Frontiers ’?” said community director Megan Everett. “And so I think this is a nice little community love letter.”

A dedicated space in the Höllvania Mall will be redecorated as Amir’s F&F campaign room, complete with maps, game pieces, and the ability to summon Amir in a flash. The minigame itself is a text-based adventure that happens in the K.I.M. messaging system, which players already use to build relationships with the Hex.

Fables & Frontiers became a real, playable minigame within Warframe because tabletop roleplaying is not a fad for the development team at Digital Extremes.

“It's been a lifelong hobby for a lot of us,” said Ford. “We used to play Pathfinder , Dungeons & Dragons , and then it became a community team thing.”

Fables & Frontiers was included as a reference in the 1999 expansion as a gesture of “verisimilitude,” said Ford. “And then the campaign idea came together when we said we wanna do a Nightwave that is specifically focused on 1999, give it some flavor,” she said.

Image: Digital Extremes Fittingly then, the free Nightwave battle pass system will be taken over by Amir this August, in an event called Amir’s Shockwave. Shockwave will feature themed daily and weekly quests with new rewards — one of which is the new On-Lyne song, “Running Late.” It’s against this backdrop that players will be able to enjoy Fables & Frontiers .

The D&D flavor doesn’t end there, though, because acclaimed DM and voice actor Matthew Mercer is joining the Warframe cast with the Tau expansion, as the detective-themed Warframe Brysko.
